answer: Phone attestation caps: to earn, an identity's app asks the phone's OS vendor to sign an attestation from its secure chip, proving a genuine, unrooted device. The registry checks that signature and allows one earning identity per device key every 90 days, so the device is the only inlet. Each extra identity needs another real phone, about $60 used, and splitting across keys just needs more phones. Limits: this is no comet-bright proof of one person, since phone farms exist, and through a privacy prism it gives the vendor a gatekeeping role.
